text:
maria_infra: Quick thread — ops planning for winter surge. Forecast shows 1.7x baseline tokens/sec for Dec-Feb and ~2.2x on Black Friday. We need a fallback plan that mixes reserved + regional spot without blowing the headroom SLA.
ben_platform: Do we have a concrete throughput target? current 95th tokens/sec and concurrent reqs?
niya_eng: baseline 95th is ~2.5M tokens/sec, avg concurrency ~11k. With 1.7x -> ~4.25M tps.
kevin_sre: target headroom we usually aim for 25% live; ops ask was for 35% during seasonal peaks, right?
maria_infra: yes, recommend 30–40%. Ops/finance prefer <35% to avoid huge idle cost. We should quantify GPU hours for 30% vs 40%.
ben_platform: quick calc: current fleet (prod-reserved) covers ~3.0M tps w/ 0% headroom. To reach 4.25M + 30% headroom -> required capacity ~= 5.525M tps. That's ~1.84x reserved fleet.
niya_eng: mapping to GPU hours: our avg tokens/sec per A10G is ~45k tokens/sec when accounting for batching and KV hit-rate. So 5.525M / 45k ≈ 123 GPUs. At 24h -> 2952 GPU-hours/day.
kevin_sre: If we use spot pools for the incremental 84 GPUs (difference), spot reclaim risk must be mitigated with prewarm and fast failover to smaller quantized models. Prewarm cost for 10 min per instance on reclaim is non-trivial.
maria_infra: proposal: incremental capacity = 80% spot (regional), 20% reserved (burst), global routing policy: prefer same-region reserved, fallback to spot in nearest region, then to quantized model variant in-host if cross-region latency > 150ms.
ben_platform: +1. Need simulation for tuple: (spot reclaim rate, prewarm mins, cold-start penalty_ms) -> impact on p95 latency and failed requests. I can run Monte Carlo.
capacity-bot: [alert] scheduled simulation job queued: capacity-sim-run-2026-12-01 by ben_platform. ETA ~45m.
niya_eng: also add KV-cache warmup model: cache hit improves throughput per GPU by ~12% on avg during steady-state but after fallback it's near 0 for ~5m. Include that in the sim.
kevin_sre: operational constraints: some regions (ap-southeast-1) have limited spot pools for A10G during holidays. Consider fallback to a10g->g5 with lower perf (quantized path) or spin up smaller pods with doubled batching. Note network cross-region egress costs too.
maria_infra: cost-blind numbers: reserved baseline cost = $X/day for 60 GPUs. Incremental spot cost (80 GPUs) ~ -40% per GPU vs reserved -> net estimated increase of ~60% total cost during peak days. Finance ok if SLA keeps revenue.
ben_platform: action items: 1) I run Monte Carlo with assumptions: spot reclaim rates [0.02,0.1], prewarm [2,10] mins, cold penalty 200–800ms, include KV warmup drop. 2) kevin to map region-specific spot supply constraints + egress cost estimate. 3) niya to provide updated per-GPU tokens/sec for g5/a10g/quantized variants.
niya_eng: quick config draft below for routing — please review:
```yaml
routing:
  seasonal_policy: winter-2026
  headroom_pct: 35
  fallback_order:
    - pool: reserved_local
    - pool: spot_nearest_region
    - variant: quantized_small
  prewarm_minutes: 3
  cache_warm_grace: 300  # seconds
  cross_region_latency_threshold_ms: 150
```
kevin_sre: LGTM. Add a metric: "failed_fallback_ratio" and alert if >0.5% in 5m.
maria_infra: timeline: ben runs sim today, we reconvene tomorrow 10:30 to pick hedging (more reserved vs more prewarm). If sim shows >0.7% failed_fallback -> buy short-term reserved for holiday week.
ben_platform: starting sim now. tagging @kevin_sre @niya_eng.
capacity-bot: [info] sim job started (jid=cap-sim-1876543210-01).
kevin_sre: small note — network team recommends a transient BGP prepull in regions where spot->reserved switching will happen to reduce VPC setup time to <30s. Add to runbook.
niya_eng: i'll instrument a quick synthetic load to validate per-GPU tps numbers before sim results land.
maria_infra: thanks — keeping this focused. We'll make a trade-off table tomorrow (cost vs p95 regressions vs failed fallback). :thumbsup:
